subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Overall passenger satisfaction (a synthesized rating/satisfaction measure derived from the per-aspect scores)

per_column.name: avg_rating
per_column.rationale: Aggregate of aspect ratings — a direct operationalization of overall satisfaction, the central focus concept.

per_column.name: rating_consistency
per_column.rationale: Std dev across aspects; a coherent facet describing how uniform a passenger's satisfaction is.

per_column.name: lowest_rated_aspect
per_column.rationale: Identifies the weakest driver of dissatisfaction — a useful diagnostic facet of the satisfaction focus.

per_column.name: satisfaction_gap
per_column.rationale: Spread/gap between best and worst aspect; directly names and characterizes the satisfaction concept.

per_column.name: review_length
per_column.rationale: Bare text length; a generic mechanical feature not centered on satisfaction, weak signal.

per_column.name: is_verified
per_column.rationale: Metadata flag; a potential predictor/segment but tangential to the satisfaction concept itself.

per_column.name: traveler_type
per_column.rationale: Segmentation variable enabling analysis of satisfaction by traveler group — supports investigation of the focus.

per_column.name: is_business_class
per_column.rationale: Class segment predictor for satisfaction differences — coherent attribute around the focus.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively cohere around a clear, data-inferable focus: overall passenger satisfaction synthesized from the existing per-aspect ratings. Several columns realize this well — avg_rating (level), rating_consistency (dispersion), satisfaction_gap (spread), and lowest_rated_aspect (dissatisfaction driver) form a genuine multi-facet structure at a useful granularity rather than a single restatement. Segmentation variables (traveler_type, is_business_class) add actionable predictor structure for investigating who is satisfied and why. The set is dragged down by two generic/tangential additions — review_length (bare text length) and is_verified (metadata flag) — which are the mechanical grab-bag elements this test penalizes. The implied focus is clearly actionable: an analyst can rank aspects, compare segments, and target the lowest-rated driver. Not a perfect score because the focus is somewhat under-differentiated (multiple columns hover close to a single 'average satisfaction' restatement) and two columns dilute coherence.
